method.inspection: Viewed every generated screenshot before choosing subsequent adaptive input. Read helper --help only; no game source, tests, docs, prior reviews, recordings, target metadata or internal game state inspected.
method.pause_limitation: Helper captured live and paused combat after each playing segment. Planning maps remained open until visibly tapped CLOSE MAP. Inspection time therefore did not continuously expose the player to combat; segmented synthetic play does not establish continuous enjoyment.

helpful_moments.observation: Centered opening fire hold removed the induction guard from view without damage.
Map gave an explicit walking route and remaining distance; later check showed Mara only 17m away after I overshot. Its pause allowed deliberate route correction.
MOVE CLOSER with 1.4m outside reach and held USE movement made the final receiver adjustment understandable; Mara recovery lit 01 and restored health.
Dash gave PHASE EVADE +75 feedback; the warden was absent after the second burst, with shield recovery visible.
Distinct memory slots, receiver names, objective changes and custodian percentages made progress legible.

frustrations_and_failures.observation: Initial straight movement ended against the induction structure. Side-lane movement then overshot the receiver and took patrol damage. Map corrected my navigation; this is an observed player difficulty, not proof of a broken route.
Small edge PATH and incoming-fire cues were harder to interpret than the map; off-screen threats were difficult to locate in portrait.
Precise fire drag required multiple corrections and reloads. End accuracy was 6%; aim technique and synthetic discrete gestures contributed, so this does not isolate a control defect.

Pillars and low cover blocked custodian shots. First bursts left every coil at 100%. A later apparently exposed view still yielded no observed reduction: I initially aimed near numbered armor rather than the lower copper winding.
I corrected downward toward copper, waited through reload and fired again, but died before verifying damage. End occurred during that segment; the last dash tap did not establish a second evade.

scores.scale: 0 unusable; 5 mixed but playable with substantial friction; 7 good with noticeable shortcomings; 10 exceptional throughout the observed scope. Scores are subjective to this single segmented emulated portrait attempt, not a physical-device certification.

reasons.overall_mobile: Completable basic interactions and three recovered memories, strong atmosphere, but navigation and precise coil combat caused repeated friction and terminal loss.
reasons.controls: Large labeled touch targets and two-contact movement/fire worked. Fine aiming and long turns needed corrections; 6% accuracy limits confidence in combat comfort.
reasons.gameplay: Receiver progression, resource recovery and dash timing provided useful decisions. Patrol pressure and obstructed coil sightlines overwhelmed this attempt. Later encounter balance is unassessed.
reasons.presentation: Cohesive cyan/amber visual language, rain, industrial environment and polished title/end panels. Audio not assessed.
reasons.usability: Handbook, explicit reach distance, paused route map and clear objective transitions helped me recover all memories. More map checks were needed than felt comfortable.
reasons.readability: Health/ammo and progress were readable at 390px; small route/threat cues, narrow world view and visually overlapping coil armor/cover made rapid interpretation harder.

limits: Synthetic paused Chromium mobile emulation; not a physical phone.

Physical phones, Safari, audio, hardware performance and continuous enjoyment remain unassessed.
